traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 167 Combretaceae: trees or shrubs, often climbing; leaves opposite, alternate or rarely whorled, simple; no stipules; flowers in spikes or racemes, mostly small; calyx tube joined to the ovary, its limb 4- to 8-lobed; petals 4 or 5 or none; stamens 4 to 10; ovary inferior, rarely half-inferior; fruit often winged (Combretum, read as a samara), rarely opening; Terminalia's drupes (Indian almond) from common knowledge.
